title: The bell comes from another house

ITEM_BELL_CLAPPER_DESC: Raske raudkeel ilma kellata. Keegi teisest majast peab selle viima.
A heavy iron clapper without its bell. Somebody from another house must carry it.
CP_BELL_TRIGGER: A visitor from another world brought the clapper.
CP_BELL_EFFECT: Kell riputati üles. Hilisematel aastatel seisab poe juures kellapost.
The bell was hung. In the later years a bell post stands by the shop.
EX_BELL_KEPT: Kellapost. Keel on teisest kohast, öeldakse. Heli on ikka omal.
A bell post. The clapper is from elsewhere, they say. The sound is its own.

origin: + { not has_item("{ITEM}") and not flag("{FLAG}") } [Mis raud see seal maas on? %% What iron is that on the ground?]

Kellakeel. Kell läks mõisaga. Keel jäi. Meie omad ei tohi seda viia, nii on vana sõna. # en: A bell clapper. The bell went with the manor. The clapper stayed. Our own may not carry it, so the old word goes.
trigger: + { has_item("{ITEM}") and not flag("{FLAG}") and visiting() } [Anna kellakeel. %% Hand over the clapper.]
Teisest majast. Siis võib. # en: From another house. Then it may be.
Kell on kuuris. Homme see heliseb. # en: The bell is in the shed. Tomorrow it rings.
+ { has_item("{ITEM}") and not flag("{FLAG}") and not visiting() } [Anna kellakeel. %% Hand over the clapper.]

Ei. Mitte sinu käest. Sõna on, et selle peab tooma keegi teisest majast. Sõbra käest võtan. # en: No. Not from you. The word is that somebody from another house must bring it. From a friend I would take it.
later: + { flag("{FLAG}") } [Kellapost poe juures. %% The bell post by the shop.]
Keel on võõras, öeldakse. Keegi tõi. Heli on ikka omal. # en: The clapper is foreign, they say. Somebody brought it. The sound is its own.
